question: Do the 2010 Jumawan, Herrera, and Jacinto NAST abstract and the 2010 BAR National Research Symposium citation refer to the same publication or sample, and what can be stated without the underlying BAR proceedings?

officialCitingPapers.citation: Vallejo and Soriano (2011), Philippine Science Letters 4(1), pp. 11-17.
officialCitingPapers.reviewed: Journal-hosted PDF, including the reference entry for the 2010 Bureau of Agricultural Research proceedings contribution and methods describing an undated 200-fish field sample.

officialCitingPapers.citation: Jumawan et al. (2011), Philippine Science Letters 4(2), pp. 103-113.
officialCitingPapers.reviewed: Journal-hosted PDF, including its reference entry for the same-titled 2010 Bureau of Agricultural Research proceedings citation and its account of the separate 36-specimen barcode series.

officialBarProceedingsExistenceLead.finding: The official DA-BAR 2011 annual report states that the 2010 National Research Symposium proceedings were produced and distributed. It does not identify this individual contribution or verify its contents.

officialNastComparison.finding: The official NAST Volume 32, Issue 1 PDF contains abstract BS-39, printed pages 80-81, with a distinct title naming source-labeled Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus and Marikina River.

sourceAccess.searchScope: Reviewed exact citation variants in the two official journal-hosted 2011 PDFs and checked an exact-title web search plus BAR/DA-domain searches. These searches did not retrieve the original contribution; they are bounded searches, not proof that no public copy exists.

bibliographyComparison.barProceedingsCitationAsPrinted: Jumawan JC, Herrera AA, Jacinto SD. Length-weight and gonado-morphometric characterization of the janitor fish Pterygoplichthis Gill, 1858 from Marikina River, Philippines: Reproduction in an invasive fish before tropical storm Ondoy. National Research Symposium-Bureau of Agricultural Research, Vol 1. Quezon City: Department of Agriculture-Republic of the Philippines; 2010: 1-15.
barCitationVariants: The 2011 matrix-model reference uses gonado-morphometric and prints Pterygoplichthis.
The 2011 DNA-barcode reference uses gonadomorphometric and also prints Pterygoplichthis.
bibliographyComparison.nastCitation: Jumawan, J. C., Herrera, A. A., & Jacinto, S. D. (2010). Length-Weight and Gonado-Morphometric Characterization of the Janitor Fish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber, 1991) From Marikina River, Philippines. NAST Transactions, 32(1), abstract BS-39, printed pp. 80-81.
distinctBibliographicAttributes: The NAST item is an official proceedings abstract in NAST Transactions, Volume 32(1), abstract BS-39, printed pages 80-81; the BAR item is cited as a National Research Symposium - Bureau of Agricultural Research proceedings contribution, Volume 1, pages 1-15.
The NAST title names Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus and does not contain the Ondoy subtitle; the BAR reference uses a genus-level spelling and includes the Ondoy subtitle.
The 2014 embryonic-development paper cites the NAST item; the two 2011 Philippine Science Letters papers cite the BAR item.
bibliographyComparison.interpretation: The citations must be represented separately because their printed bibliographic details differ. Without the original BAR proceedings contribution, it is not possible to determine whether it reproduces, expands, corrects, or is independent of the NAST abstract.

sampleLineage.barItemToNastAbstract: Unresolved. Shared authors and topic support a related-publication lead only; the full BAR item, identifiers, dates, methods, and sample list were unavailable for direct comparison.
sampleLineage.barItemTo2011MatrixModel: The model paper cites the BAR item and reports 200 field-collected fish for fecundity estimation, but gives no collection period, gear, station, vouchers, or specimen IDs. The citation does not prove those 200 fish are the BAR sample.
sampleLineage.barItemTo2011BarcodeSeries: The barcode paper cites the BAR item and reports a separate 36-specimen Marikina series with vouchers/accessions. No crosswalk identifies these specimens as part of the BAR contribution.
sampleLineage.barItemTo2014EmbryonicStudy: The 2014 paper cites the NAST abstract, not the BAR citation in the reviewed reference list. Its 36 adult fish have no specimen link to the BAR item or the model paper.
sampleLineage.barItemTo2016LifeHistoryCohort: No BAR citation or specimen-level link to the 2016 aggregate 1,133-fish sample was found in the reviewed evidence. The 2016 paper links its sex-specific 2014 and 2015 studies; this does not resolve the earlier BAR sample.
sampleLineage.decision: Do not merge these publication records, count the 200 fish as a distinct sample, or infer overlap/independence with any other Marikina cohort until the source or specimen-level identifiers are available.

evidenceDecision.decision: Register the BAR reference as a citation-only research lead distinct from the NAST abstract. Keep the relationship among the two 2010 bibliographic items and all Marikina study samples unresolved. No app-facing biological assertion is supported.

nonClaims: Different citations do not prove independent publications, distinct data, or separate fish samples; the BAR primary proceedings contribution was not retrieved.
The official BAR annual report confirms proceedings production/distribution only, not this contribution’s presence, text, authorship, pages, or data.
The genus spelling Pterygoplichthis in the 2011 reference lists is preserved as printed and does not establish a taxonomic identification.
The NAST abstract’s source-reported species label is not transferred to the BAR citation, 2011 model sample, barcode records, 2014 adult fish, or 2016 cohort.
No capture date, method, location below Marikina River, count, vouchers, coordinates, current presence, abundance, or independent occurrence is established by this citation crosswalk.
nextActions: Keep the original BAR proceedings contribution on a retrieval queue; use only a legitimate public catalog, library copy, or author/publisher-provided access if it becomes available.

If the original item is retrieved, compare its exact text, publication statement, field dates, method, counts, and any voucher or accession identifiers directly with the NAST abstract and related studies.
Until then, keep the NAST and BAR records separate as bibliography entries but do not claim that they are independent studies or independent fish samples.
